OBJECTIVES
EQUIPMENT REQUIRED
This lesson will explain why electric current flows easily through some materials and does not flow easily through others.
INTRODUCTIONM

We will start by looking at the characteristics of conductors, the materials that are used to connect every type of electric circuit. We will see how material choice and other physical factors affect a material's ability to conduct current.
We will next move on to insulators, and their characteristics. We will show how voltage can affect insulators and why insulators are important for safety reasons.
The lesson concludes with a brief introduction to semiconductor materials. These materials are vitally important to the ever-growing electronics and computer industries.
Let's begin the lesson on CONDUCTORS, INSULATORS AND SEMICONDUCTORS.
LESSON MENU
We have seen that every type of material is made up of atoms and that electrons from these atoms are required for current to flow.
DISCUSSION

A conductor is any material that will allow a substantial current to flow with even a small voltage applied. Remember that voltage is a form of electrical pressure that pushes electrons through a path. If there is no voltage applied to a circuit, there cannot be any current flow.
Copper is one of the best conductors. Copper is conducting current in the computer you are now using!
Why is copper a good conductor? This question can be answered by looking at the atomic makeup of a copper atom.

Every copper atom has 29 electrons. However, due to laws of physics, only 28 of these electrons are held tightly in orbit around the nucleus. The 29th electron is only loosely bound to the nucleus and requires only a small force to be moved. This outer electron is known as a Valence Electron.
DEFINITION

VALENCE ELECTRONS - The atoms of different materials all have different numbers of electrons. However, these electrons can only exist at certain energy levels around the nucleus. Each energy level is like a "shelf" that can only hold a specific number of electrons.

Once one of these levels is full, electrons start filling the next higher shelf. The outermost energy level of any atom is called the valence level and the electrons it contains are called valence electrons. The number of electrons in the valence level determines how well a material conducts.

Since the single valence electron of a copper atom is easily moved, copper acts as a good conductor. Other materials such as silver, gold, and aluminum have similar atomic properties and are also good conductors.

We must understand that current flowing through a conductor does not REMOVE electrons from the conductor. A good conductor only allows electrons to be easily transferred from atom to atom. The electrons that make up the current are always supplied by the source.

There is no type of material that has zero resistance unless special conditions are met. Under normal circumstances all materials have some opposition to current flow. Since we are looking at conductors, we will concentrate on the factors that affect conductor resistance.

The actual resistance of any conductor depends upon three primary factors plus temperature, which we will consider later. The first factor is obviously the type of material, for example, whether it is copper, silver, aluminum, etc.

There is one more factor we have not yet looked at which can affect resistance. This factor is temperature. Until now, all the exercises we have done have assumed that temperature is constant, at a room temperature of 20
Celsius. However, as temperature changes resistance also changes.
To understand why temperature affects conductor resistance, we must look at what happens inside the conductor as temperature changes.
Scientists have determined that the lowest possible temperature is approximately -273
C. At this temperature it is thought that all random internal motion of atoms and molecules inside a conductor stops. This means at -273
C every conductor would have zero resistance.
C there is some motion of the particles within the conductor. This motion contributes to the resistance of the conductor because the electrons that pass through are "bumped" by the moving particles.

As the temperature continues to increase, there is more internal motion within the conductor. This means there is more opposition to current flow within the conductor and the conductor resistance increases.
The fact that conductor resistance increases with temperature means that conductors have a positive temperature coefficient .
Conductor resistance increases as temperature increases.
DEFINITION
TEMPERATURE COEFFICIENT - The temperature coefficient is a number that is used to show how temperature is related to the resistance of a material. This value may be either positive or negative.

The resistance of a material with a positive temperature coefficient increases as temperature increases. The resistance of a material with a negative temperature coefficient decreases as temperature increases.

In most situations where conductors are used, insulators are also present. The primary reasons for this are safety of the people using the conductors, and prevention of faults within the circuit.
DISCUSSION

Insulators are materials that normally do not allow current to flow through them. This is because the atoms and molecules of insulating materials have strongly bound electrons, and it is very difficult to move these electrons to create current flow.
A large force is required to move these electrons!
The jacket around any electrical cord is an example of an insulator. When current is flowing through the wires within the cord, the insulating jacket has no current flow through it.

Although insulators do not normally permit current to flow through them, it is possible to get any insulator to conduct. To cause an insulating material to conduct, a very high voltage must be applied to it.
If we think of voltage as electrical pressure, by increasing voltage across an insulator, we create an increasing force on the atomic structure of the insulator.

As this force gets larger, it can eventually become high enough to remove strongly bound electrons from their atomic orbits. When this happens, the insulator will conduct current. This causes something called INSULATOR BREAKDOWN.

The value of applied voltage at which an insulator will start to conduct current is called the Breakdown Voltage. Every type of insulating material has a breakdown voltage, but the actual values vary from material to material.

The air around us is a common insulator but even air has a breakdown voltage. You may have seen evidence of this if you have ever received a shock by touching a doorknob after walking across a dry, carpeted room.
KLLKLRLL
KKLKRLRK
RLRLLKLLR
In this situation, the insulating air breaks down but you don't get a shock until your hand is very close to the doorknob.

The fact that the shock does not happen until your hand is very close to the doorknob shows an important point about insulators. The breakdown voltage of an insulator depends upon the thickness, or distance, across the insulator.
The thicker the insulator, the higher the breakdown voltage.
As any insulator gets thicker, it takes more voltage to cause it to breakdown.
Breakdown voltage of a specific insulator is expressed as applied voltage per insulator thickness.

The accepted value of breakdown voltage for air is 30,000 volts/centimeter, or 30 kV/cm. The value for glass is 900 kV/cm. This means that glass requires 30 times more applied voltage to breakdown than air does, so glass is a much better insulator than air. Glass is a much better insulator than air!!!!!!!!
Glass is a much better insulator than air!

2. Every insulator has a breakdown voltage. This value is the voltage that will force the insulator to conduct current and is usually very high. The breakdown voltage for insulators depends on the atomic makeup of the material.

4. Insulators are very important for safety and proper system operation. They should be checked regularly and replaced if necessary.

Semiconductors are materials that have resistance characteristics that show a combination of the properties of conductors and insulators.
DISCUSSION

A semiconductor can act as a conductor or as an insulator, but its characteristics are controlled electrically. This means that semiconductors can allow current to flow at one time, then block current flow at another time.
Since the circuit designer can control this action, semiconductors are powerful devices. There are many semiconductor devices in this computer in the form of integrated circuits.

The most common semiconductor material is silicon, but others such as germanium and gallium arsenide are also popular. Most semiconductor materials have four valence electrons, which contributes to their conduction properties.
Silicon is the most popular semiconductor!

Most semiconductors are responsive to changes in temperature. However, unlike conductors, semiconductors have negative temperature coefficients. This means that their resistance decreases as temperature increases. The resistance of semiconductors decrease as temperature increases.......................................
The resistance of semiconductors decrease as temperature increases.
Semiconductors will be covered in much greater detail in upcoming lessons.
